plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered blooms in many forms, including pompons, spiders, and decorative types. It thrives in cool autumn temperatures and is a staple of fall gardens and floral displays.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-autumn to early winter in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; native to East Asia, with major cultivation in China, Japan, and Europe
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are the national flower of Japan, and the annual Chrysanthemum Festival there celebrates the flower's importance, with the Imperial seal featuring a stylized 16-petal chrysanthemum.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large, graceful tree that bursts into clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers just before the leaves emerge. In full bloom, the tree and the carpet of fallen petals beneath it create a striking sight along streets and in parks.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring (October to December in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia (Grafton, Sydney, Brisbane), Argentina, and Brazil
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City' because it has tens of thousands of jacaranda trees, and local folklore says a flower falling on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub that blooms in autumn, earlier than its relative Camellia japonica. It produces delicate, slightly fragrant single or semi-double flowers with prominent golden stamens, and it attracts late-season pollinators such as bees.
plants.location: Native to Japan; grown in the southeastern United States, Europe, Japan, and temperate regions of Australia
plants.funFact: Sasanqua camellia petals fall individually, whereas many Camellia japonica flowers drop whole, and the species is related to the tea plant, Camellia sinensis.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: A bulbous perennial from South Africa that sends up leafless stalks topped with spidery, sparkling pink flowers with wavy petals. It brings a vivid splash of color to gardens when most other perennials are fading.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn, typically October to November in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the Eastern Cape and Drakensberg region of South Africa; naturalized in gardens in the UK, Europe, and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: The petals have a crystalline, glittering surface that sparkles in sunlight, which is why related Nerine species are often called 'Guernsey lilies' or 'diamond lilies.'
